Subject: AcmeHealth - follow-up: private VPC/data handling recap and next steps

Hi Priya - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of requirements we captured
- Data types: PII and limited PHI (patient identifiers, timestamps, and hashed IDs) processed by inference requests.
- Residency: customer requires all inference traffic to terminate in their private VPC in us-west-2; no tokenized text may leave the VPC.
- Egress: strict no-egress policy to the public internet from the model serving subnet; peering or private interconnect preferred.
- Logging & retention: audit logs must be shipped to ACME-managed S3 (or equivalent) and retained for 7 years; ability to redact PII in logs required.
- Key management: KMS/HSM integration required for encryption at rest and in transit.
- On-prem/air-gapped: long-term interest in an on-prem or air-gapped deployment for isolated sites.

Open items / asks for ACME before we share a proposed architecture
1) Please share your network diagram (VPC/subnet/peering/MTU constraints) and any existing firewall/NAT constraints.
2) Confirm whether ACME can accept a private peering connection to Redwood-managed endpoints or if you require a fully customer-hosted/private deployment.
3) Upload your completed security questionnaire and SOC2 report (if available).
4) Key rotation/segregation requirements for KMS and any legal/regulatory constraints we should know about.

Next steps
- If you can share the network diagram and questionnaire, our infra team will map out a no-egress design that meets your retention/KMS needs.
- I'll loop in Rishi (solutions) and Logan (infra) to produce a preliminary dataflow diagram by EOD Thursday.
- Can you confirm availability for a technical review on Friday 3/19 at 10am PT?

Thanks - we want to be sure any proposed design respects ACME's no-egress requirement and gives you clear controls over retention and logging.

Best,

Thanks Marissa - great summary. A few clarifications and attaching the documents you asked for.

Clarifications
- Confirmed: the data flows you captured are correct. We process PHI in a limited way (patient identifiers + encounter metadata) - those cannot leave our VPC unencrypted and must be accessible only to authorized subnets.
- Egress: we cannot allow any outbound NAT to the public internet from the serving subnet. All traffic must traverse our transit gateway/private peering to partner services.
- Retention: logs must be retained for 7 years; we are comfortable with logs being delivered to our S3 bucket with server-side encryption using our KMS key.
- KMS: we require customer-managed CMKs (AWS KMS) with key policies that allow Redwood's service principal limited decrypt/encrypt usage only in the context of serving.
- On-prem: for one of our regulated sites, we require an air-gapped deployment - timeline TBD but please advise feasibility and high-level options.

Attached: ACMEHealth_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, acme-network-diagram.drawio

We're available for a technical sync on Friday 3/19 at 10am PT - adding Jake (network lead) to the thread; he'll bring the detailed VPC constraints.

Thanks,

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: AcmeHealth - technical notes & proposed options

Marissa / Logan - quick internal notes after reviewing Priya's questionnaire and diagram:

1) Architecture options (feasible):
  - Private VPC with AWS PrivateLink / Interface VPC endpoints: Redwood runs model serving in a private subnet in the customer VPC (Private deployment). No public egress.
  - VPC peering / Transit Gateway: Redwood endpoints in a partner VPC peered to ACME; egress disabled and route tables restricted to ACME-managed prefixes. Requires agreement on routes and MTU.
  - On-prem / air-gapped appliance: possible but will require custom packaging and physical deployment; propose as long-term phase 2.

2) KMS / key management:
  - We support using customer CMKs via cross-account grants and IAM roles for server-side encryption. Will require a limited role that Redwood assumes for encryption operations; KMS key policy examples attached (I will add them to the dataflow doc).

3) Logging & retention:
  - Audit logs (request metadata) can be pushed to ACME S3 via VPC endpoints or S3 bucket policies. We can implement PII redaction in logs prior to delivery (configurable). Retention policies can be set using S3 lifecycle + legal hold as required.

4) Network / egress controls:
  - No-NAT design: ensure no Internet gateway on serving subnet; use VPC endpoints and peered paths only. We'll need Jake to confirm whether he can accept interface endpoints or requires full on-prem peering.

Action items
- I'll produce a preliminary dataflow diagram and a list of control mappings (SOC2 controls, encryption, logging) by EOD today.
- Marissa: please confirm whether we should prepare an on-prem cost estimate or scope that out after the initial VPC design.
- Marissa: schedule the Fri 10am PT call and include Jake + Priya; I'll be on the call.
